frequency_question: How often do central banks implement incremental or ad-hoc reserve ratio requirements (such as an incremental cash reserve ratio or equivalent secondary liquidity sequestering tool) when facing sudden liquidity overhangs?
membership_rule: Members are central banks in major emerging economies (e.g., RBI, Bank Indonesia, Bank of Thailand, Central Bank of Brazil, Bank Negara Malaysia) that faced discrete structural liquidity gluts (e.g., from massive FX inflows or government spending reversals) and had the statutory power to deploy incremental reserve requirements between 2004 and 2026. Excluded are developed market central banks lacking statutory reserve ratio mechanisms or countries experiencing hyperinflation where reserve ratios are structurally irrelevant.

cases.name: RBI CRR hike (normal cycle, not iCRR)
Bank Indonesia secondary reserve requirement (GWM) adjustment
People's Bank of China targeted/incremental RR adjustments
Central Bank of Brazil compulsory deposit requirement tightening
Bank of Thailand unremunerated reserve requirement (URR) on capital inflows
Bank Indonesia secondary reserve requirement adjustment

provenance_note: 8 cases named, 10 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.2x)
coverage_note: 8 named; believed roughly 10 in total across major comparable Asian and Latin American jurisdictions in the timeframe.
known_gaps: Excludes minor adjustments in smaller frontier economies lacking transparent central bank policy archives.
skeleton: Decomposed into major emerging market central bank liquidity management episodes where liquidity overhang exceeded standard open market operation capacity by more than 1% of system deposits, triggering structural reserve tool consideration.
multiplier: 8 hits out of 10 identified major systemic liquidity overhang episodes across target emerging market jurisdictions where the structural tool was legally available and actively debated.
validity_reason: Statutory central bank frameworks and liquidity management toolkits evolve slowly over multi-year horizons; the legal and operational friction for deploying reserve ratios remains stable.
